title: Power in Numbers
summary:
Power in Numbers
As if an extension of the arm of US bureaucracy, the tanker market is slugging along relentlessly with freight levels capable of beating down even the most optimistic. Unlike the US Congress which takes summer recess for the month of August, tankers are here to stay. However, after July's routing of positive returns on both the dirty and clean side ‐ which left earnings on some voyages with negative earnings ‐ the futilitarian thought process may have many shipowners looking for a break from what could be a long month ahead.

children.title: Does it Add Up?
children.summary: The use of triangulation provides owners with the ability to push the utilization of their vessel over 100%, increasing the timecharter equivalent (TCE) for the duration of the voyage. For example, a VLCC making the standard voyage from the Arabian Gulf to LOOP would load and discharge a single cargo before returning to the Arabian Gulf for another voyage after roughly 76 days round‐trip.

children.title: Effectively Earning
children.summary: So even as the assessed timecharter equivalent dips below $0 per day or struggles to match break‐even costs, owner's are not willing to throw in the towel yet. Simple freight economics may point the current market to lay‐ups and premature scrapping but there is more than meets the eye.
